era: PlayStation / PlayStation 2 / Xbox / PSP / Nintendo DS / Xbox 360 / Wii
summary: Acquire, K2, and FromSoftware's ninja stealth-action series, including the PlayStation originals, expanded ports, handheld entries, and later Xbox/Wii experiments.

entries.title: Tenchu: Stealth Assassins
entries.definitive_edition: Western PlayStation release, with Shinobi Gaisen as a presentation supplement

emulation.notes: DuckStation can improve PS1 image quality with PGXP/upscaling while preserving the original release.

primary.why: The Western PlayStation release added two levels, alternating mission layouts, technical improvements, a level editor, and a cheat menu over the original Japanese launch. It is the best main route for English play and fuller gameplay content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the North American PlayStation disc on DuckStation or original hardware; use PGXP/upscaling if emulating, and avoid the censored UK build if you want the uncensored item set.

secondary.exclusive_content: Japan-only re-release presentation with a new opening
secondary.what_to_play: Check Shinobi Gaisen only for its Japan-only presentation differences after playing the Western release.
secondary.why: It reissued the Western-expanded version in Japan with a new opening, but the main mission content overlaps the primary route.

all_releases.reason: skip: historically first, but the later Western version added missions, alternate layouts, polish, editor tools, and cheats.

all_releases.fidelity: Expanded Western PlayStation release with added levels, alternate layouts, technical improvements, level editor, and cheat menu.
Japan-only re-release of the Western-expanded version with a new opening.
all_releases.reason: secondary: presentation curiosity, not required for the main playthrough.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The Japanese Shinobi Gaisen has a unique opening, while the Western release is the practical English route with the expanded mission set; use Shinobi Gaisen only as a supplement.

entries.title: Tenchu: Shinobi Hyakusen

emulation.notes: Use PS1 emulation for image cleanup; the game remains a Japan-only challenge expansion.

primary.why: Shinobi Hyakusen is a standalone Japan-only expansion built from one hundred selected user-created levels made with Shinobi Gaisen's level editor. It has no other documented platform route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese PlayStation disc on original hardware or DuckStation; expect non-story challenge levels rather than a new campaign.

all_releases.fidelity: Original standalone PlayStation expansion using the same engine and fundamentals as the first game.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or localized release exists.

entries.title: Tenchu 2: Birth of the Stealth Assassins
entries.definitive_edition: Japanese PlayStation release for completeness; North American release for English

emulation.notes: Use DuckStation with PGXP/upscaling for the PS1 release; choose region based on language versus completeness preference.

primary.why: The Japanese PlayStation release came after the North American and European versions and added further graphical/technical improvements plus expanded level-editor objects. It is the most complete technical version, while the North American release remains the best fully English route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Japanese PlayStation release on DuckStation for the most complete technical build; use the North American disc instead if English text and voices matter more than the extra Japanese editor/technical improvements.

secondary.exclusive_content: English localization without the European censorship changes
secondary.what_to_play: Use this version if you want the story in English.
secondary.why: The Japanese release has the technical/editor edge, but the North American release is the cleanest localized route.

all_releases.reason: secondary: best English route, but lacks the later Japanese technical/editor improvements.

all_releases.fidelity: PAL release with censorship changes including reduced blood/decapitations and shuriken replacement.
all_releases.reason: skip: localized, but source-documented censorship makes it worse for archival completeness.

all_releases.fidelity: Later Japanese release with further graphical/technical improvements and expanded level-editor objects.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Japanese release has the technical/editor edge, North America has the cleanest English route, and Europe has censorship changes.
